title: Formal Foundations of Spatiotemporal Compliance and Distributed System Integrity
abstract_snippet: Automated compliance verification in cyber-physical environments is often performed using heuristic anomaly detection or probabilistic inference methods. While such approaches have proven effective in simple operating environments, they provide little theoretical guarantee for complex, contested, or distributed settings where adversaries or failures may simultaneously impact the system’s state. paragraphs_inventory.text_snippet: Automated compliance verification in cyber-physical environments is increasingly deployed in institutional settings ranging from campus access control to industrial safety monitoring.

Reliable compliance verification requires more than empirical performance metrics. In cyber-physical environments governed by safety or regulatory constraints, the verification logic itself must possess internally consistent mathematical semantics.

These assumptions motivate the choice of the mathematical machinery below; before introducing behavioral axioms, we briefly describe the topological, metric, and temporal spaces over which the system is defined, following spatial logics in b16 .
Having defined the underlying mathematical spaces, we now construct the formal spatiotemporal system model.
